doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
doc.interviewee: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams

chapter: Williams on guitar technique and prison
title: Williams buys his first guitar for four dollars
summary: Asked where he was born, Williams says Zachary, and tells how a white woman sold him her son's guitar for $4 after he failed with a cheap first one.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: This is my home in Zachary. Mm-hmm. Yes. I don't know Mr. Anderson Place. Mm-hmm. And we moved from Zachary in 28, nearby down there to Zion City. And we've been there ever since. Well, I moved over here on there. Skyward over there. Mm-hmm. But I made it up in my mind to buy me a guitar one day. First guitar that I bought it, the string was sitting upon it so high until you had to take hand-match it down and try to get a sound out. Yeah. Yeah. A fella sold it to me for a darn my head. I gave him a darn my head for it. Well, I found a little bit of a bump in the long run until I thought I had lunch. Well, I did lunch a few notes on it, but there wasn't nothing much I could do with it. And a couple of ladies working for a white lady. As she seen I was trying to learn, she said, my boss, Madam, just got a guitar down there. And she bought her board to take music lessons. But he's not interested in you. She said, come down there, she may sell it to you. So I did do that. I went down there. It was one of those high-priced guitars. Try some of that? It was one of those high-priced guitars, you know?
